sent_to_model:
Dana Okoye asked in #maintenance on the club Slack how to winterize her Yanmar herself, and Bev has tagged me. Hector has already told her to run green automotive antifreeze through it, which needs correcting before she does it this weekend. Please draft a reply in that thread walking her through the job in a sensible order. My notes are below. Dana is a quick study, so no hand-holding, but she is new to diesels. Leave it as a draft; I want to read it over before it goes up.

- 3GM30F is freshwater cooled, heat exchanger. Two sides. Coolant side just needs a strength check with a hydrometer, good to about -20F if 50/50. Raw water side is what freezes and cracks.
- Pink propylene glycol RV/marine antifreeze for raw water and domestic water. About 2 gal for engine, 2-3 for water system; estimates only, buy enough to complete manufacturer winterizing procedures and verify winter protection. About $6/gal at West Marine or Walmart.
- Order - warm engine, change oil and filter while warm, top fuel tank, add stabilizer, run 10 min to get it through. Then raw water flush. Capture all winterizing discharge for appropriate disposal, not into the river. Set up exhaust collection before starting; helper watches flow and collection. Collect water-system discharge too.
- Raw-water sequence - seacock closed; strainer feeds antifreeze at idle; pump kept wet; engine off after completion; seacock stays closed. Engine and antifreeze manufacturers' procedures; discharged mixture checked for required winter protection, not just pink colour.
- Spare impeller, keep one aboard. Pull the old one if she wants and inspect, don't run dry.
- Water heater bypass valve on that Catalina, behind the companionway steps. Switch off the water-heater breaker before draining; leave it off until refilled in spring. Drain tank first or she wastes 6 gal of pink.
- Christmas freeze a few years back, three boats on C dock cracked exhaust elbows or strainers. All had skipped or rushed the raw water side.
- Ethylene glycol (green) is toxic and isn't rated for the raw water system. Neither green nor pink antifreeze belongs in the river; raw water discharge exits through the exhaust. Correct Hector gently, he's a good guy.
- $465 is not a ripoff but she can do it in 2-3 hours with a helper.
- Offer to come down to the boat Saturday morning if she wants a second set of hands.

(About me: retired Navy officer, 66, Norfolk, Virginia. Length: all the messages together should come to roughly 400-800 words.)

Okay, first winter as a boat owner and I am a little out of my depth. Bought Sea Wren (2003 Catalina 30, Yanmar 3GM30F) in June, keeping her in the water at our slips. The yard quoted me $465 to winterize the engine and water system. Is this something I can realistically do myself in an afternoon? I've changed the oil once with Hector's help. What do I need, what order, and what can actually go wrong if I mess it up? Not trying to cheap out, I just want to understand my own boat.
[s04] message in #maintenance | 2026-11-07T21:30:00 | from hector.ruiz | reply to [s03]
Totally doable. I just run a jug of the green automotive stuff through mine every year, never had a problem. Takes 20 min. Don't overthink it.
